extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and geometers studying classical constructions of conic sections and trajectories (readers of Newton/Principia)
extracted.subtask_description: Geometric constructions and existence/uniqueness results for conic sections (trajectories) determined by combinations of given points, given tangents, and given proportional relations among segment-products; includes transformation lemmas that reduce problems to simpler cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVIII — rectangle-ratio tangency criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a trapezium (or quadrilateral with two opposite sides regarded) and a point P from which four lines to the sides are drawn, if the rectangle of the lines to one pair of opposite sides (PQ × PR) is to the rectangle of the lines to the other pair (PS × PT) in a given ratio, then the point P touches (is a point of tangency to) the conic section described about the trapezium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction/argument: consider auxiliary parallels through vertices, use ratios produced by given angles of triangles PQq, PRr, PSs, PTt to show PQ×PR : PS×PT is given; demonstrate that the intersection of diagonals/coincidence yields the point P on the conic. Scholium: "conicae sectionis" is taken broadly to include straight-line sections through the cone's vertex and circular sections parallel to the base; degenerate cases (lines, circle, parallels, points at infinity) are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary to Lemma XVIII — rectangle vs. square condition for tangency
rubrics_metrics.description: If three lines PQ, PR, PS from P to three fixed position lines AB, CD, AC (each in given angles) are such that the rectangle under two of the lines (PQ × PR) is to the square of the third (PS^2) in a given ratio, then the point P lies on the conic section which is tangent to the given lines AB, CD, AC; and conversely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how, as diagonals or sides coalesce, the conic becomes tangent to those lines (i.e., when two intersection points coincide the secants become tangents). Uses limiting arguments and the idea that when certain products/squares equal in given ratio, tangency results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XIX — construction/existence of point P for given product-ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Given four fixed lines AB, CD, AC, BD and four prescribed angles at which lines PQ, PR, PS, PT must meet those fixed lines, there exists a point P such that the rectangle under PQ and PR is to the rectangle under PS and PT in a given ratio; moreover, P can be located by elementary constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction method: take any line through one vertex (say A H) and consider its intersections with opposite sides; compute ratios of distances produced by given angles, subtract/add to obtain the required ratios (PQ:PS etc.), and thereby locate P. Corollary: by varying positions of some given points to infinity, one obtains loci (parabola, hyperbola, ellipse, or circle) depending on occurrence of special configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XX — parallelogram tangency and constant abscissa-ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If any parallelogram ASPQ with opposite double angles at A and P is tangent to a given conic section in two points K and L, and the infinitely produced sides AQ and AS meet that same conic in Q' and S' etc., then the abscissal parts PR and PT (parts of certain sides) are always to one another in a given ratio; conversely, if those parts are in a given ratio, then the constructed point D will touch the conic passing through the four given points A,B,C,P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives two cases in the proof: construct parallels through intersection points and apply Lemma XVII to relate rectangles; uses similarity of trapezia and coinciding diagonals to force contact. Corollaries derive practical tangency tests and converse constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary to Lemma XX — tangency test via proportional segments
rubrics_metrics.description: If BD meets PQ in r, and on PQ one takes Pt so that PR:Pt = Pr:pt, then Bt is tangent to the conic at B. Conversely, if Bt is tangent and BD, CD meet at some D, then PR:PT = Pr:pt etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a concrete proportional-segment criterion to test or produce a tangent at a given point using ratios on intersecting secants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary (Lemma XX) — two conics intersect in at most four points
rubrics_metrics.description: A conic section cannot intersect another conic section in more than four points: if two conic sections were to pass through five common points, contradictions in ratios (and earlier lemmas) follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses previous proportionality lemmas to show that assuming five intersections leads to equalities forcing impossible coincidences (contradicting assumptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXI — moving-pole construction: generating a conic from constant-angle chords
rubrics_metrics.description: If from two fixed poles B and C two mobile lines BM and CM are drawn so that their intersection M moves along a given straight line MN (i.e., M describes MN), and from M one draws through given fixed angles lines BD and CD meeting the prior lines at D, then the locus of the intersection D describes a conic through B and C. Conversely, if BD and CD through a movable D describe a conic through fixed B and C and the angles DBM and DCM are always equal to given angles, then the moving intersection M of BM and CM will always lie on the given straight line MN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses similarity of triangles formed by fixed and moving points; gives a construction and the converse; used to convert angle-rotation constructions to conic loci. Practical use: when a moving point M is constrained by equal angles, the corresponding D generated by intersection of lines with given angles is constrained to lie on a conic through B and C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XXII (Problem XIV) — construct conic through five given points
rubrics_metrics.description: Given five points A, B, C, P, D, construct the conic (trajectory) passing through them: choose any two of the points as poles (e.g. B, C), through the third (A) draw parallels to the lines joining the poles to the other points, then from the two poles draw infinitely many lines through the fifth point D, intersect the previously drawn parallels to obtain points T,R, and then choose proportional segments on PT and PR to locate a point d; the locus of d (as the auxiliary lines vary) is the required conic; in the limit when auxiliary lines vanish d coincides with D and the conic passes through all five points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two constructions are given (a primary one using parallels and proportional intercepts, and an alternative using rotating angle-applications about poles and marking intersections M,N whose chord intersection with a fixed line gives the conic point). Emphasizes limiting argument: letting auxiliary intersections coalesce yields exact passage through the given fifth point. This is the classical five-point existence/constructive uniqueness result for conics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XXIII (Problem XV) — construct conic through four points with given tangent at one point
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a tangent HB with contact point B and three other points C, D, P, construct the conic passing through C,D,P and tangent to HB at B: construct parallelogram BSPQ with PS || BH and PQ || BC, intersect BD with the appropriate sides to get T and R, then choose any parallel to TR and cut off on PQ and PS segments proportional to PR and PT respectively; intersection of the two constructed lines (from C r and B t) locates a point d on the conic. Alternative construction: rotate the given angle about the poles and use a fixed radius rotation to obtain intersections M,N whose envelope gives the desired conic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two cases considered: when tangent and points are in certain positions one construction; if tangent exterior another construction involving harmonic/proportional relations. Notes that the contact point A found may lie between or outside the given tangent intercepts, yielding two possible conics (duplicity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XXIV (Problem XVI) — construct conic through three points tangent to two given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two tangents HI, KL and three points B,C,D, construct the conic passing through B,C,D and tangent to both HI and KL: for any two of the points draw the infinite tangents meeting HI and KL at H,K and I,L respectively; cut HR and KS so that HR:KR is the mean proportional between BH and HD etc.; the intersection points A and P of the line joining these mean-proportional points with tangents are the contact points of the desired conic, from which the trajectory is then constructed as in prior problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces assumed contact points to relations among rectangles and mean proportionals deriving from conic properties; careful selection of which segment intervals to bisect (or take mean proportionals) is necessary; the construction works whether the auxiliary points lie between or outside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma (Transmutation of figures) — affine-like transformation lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: A prescription for transforming any figure of a given kind into another figure of the same kind: take two arbitrary parallel lines A O and B L cutting a chosen baseline AB; from any point G of the original figure draw a line GD parallel to AO to meet AB at D; then from a chosen pole O draw OD meeting BL at g; performing this mapping for all points yields a new figure; tangency and incidence relations are preserved and analytic order (degree) of curves is preserved (lines map to lines, conics to conics, circles to circles, higher-order curves to same order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that tangency is preserved under this mapping; provides an algebraic justification showing that if AD & DG had certain dimensional ascents in an equation, the transformed variables a d & dg ascend in the same way so order is preserved. Practical use: reduces difficult problems by transforming converging lines to parallels, hyperbolas/parabolas/ellipses into simpler forms (e.g., ellipse to circle) where construction is easier, then invert the transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XXV (Problem XVII) — construct conic through two points tangent to three given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two points and three tangent lines (positions given), transform the figure so that two of the tangents become parallel; in the transformed figure the tangents reduce to two parallel lines and a third tangent parallel to the line through the two given points, complete the parallelogram and take three constructed mean-square/rectangular segments (hc, ic, ke etc.) that yield contact points c,d,e; transfer these back by inverse transformation to locate contacts in original figure and then construct the conic through the two points touching the three lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method relies on the transmutation lemma to reduce to the simpler parallel-tangent case; explicit recipe for computing the contact points in the reduced figure is given using sums of squares and rectangles in specific proportions (these are computed by applying conic relationships). The construction may be impossible in certain ordered positional cases (e.g., one of the given points between two tangents and the other outside).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XXVI (Problem XVIII) — construct conic through one given point tangent to four given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a point and four tangents in given positions, construct the conic through the point and tangent to the four lines: choose intersections of pairs of tangents and draw an infinite auxiliary line through their common intersection to serve as the first ordinate radius (apply the transmutation lemma), thereby converting the problem to the prior problem (two points three tangents); transfer back by inverse operations to obtain the required trajectory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recipe: take common intersection of two tangents, draw an infinite line through it and use it as the ordinate radius; after the transmutation two of the tangents become parallel making application of Problem XVII possible; the inverse-transformation returns the solution to the original configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXIII (cutting a line in a given ratio yields a point on a given line)
rubrics_metrics.description: If from given positions AC and BD lines are drawn to variable points A and B and a segment CD joining indeterminate points is cut in a given ratio, then the intersection point K so obtained will lie on a particular line of given position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: let AC and BD meet at E; take BG such that BE:AE = given and keep ED equal to EG; cut CF in the given ratio to locate L, join L to K etc. The lemma gives a way to ensure that a constructed point with a prescribed ratio along CD will be located on a specified line — useful in many of the subsequent constructions that require cutting segments in particular ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXIV — semidiameter as mean proportional
rubrics_metrics.description: If two tangents AF and GB to a conic are parallel (positions given) and a third tangent EF meets them, then the semidiameter (CD) parallel to the two tangents is the mean proportional between the segments cut off on the parallels by the points of contact and the third tangent interposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a proportionality relation: AF : CD :: CD : BG (in continuous proportion), derived from properties of conjugate diameters and similar triangles formed by tangency and conjugate diameters. Corollaries: when additional symmetric configurations occur one can deduce alignment of certain chord-lines through the center, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXV — abscissa-proportion relations from parallelogram tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sides of a parallelogram (extended infinitely) are tangent to a conic and abscissae are taken on a fifth tangent, then the abscissa at one side is to the adjacent side as the corresponding opposite abscissa is to its adjacent side (specific proportional relations are given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lemma yields proportional relationships among abscissae taken from intersections of tangents and parallelogram sides; corollaries show equalities of rectangles (KQ×ME = Kh×MF etc.) and produce a method to locate the center (intersection of bisectors) when certain bisected chords are joined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XXVII (Problem XIX) — construct conic tangent to five given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given five lines (positions of tangents), construct the conic tangent to all five: form a quadrilateral bounded by any four of the tangents, bisect its diagonals to get their bisection points, join the bisection points — the line through these bisection points passes through the center of the sought conic; find the center O as intersection of bisector loci for two choices of quadrilaterals; draw a line through O at the required offset so that the line is simultaneously tangent to the desired conic and to one of the given tangents; intersect and transfer contact points by parallelling and intersections to obtain all contact points and finally construct the conic as in Problem XIV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholium: problems that give centers or asymptotes are encompassed; asymptote is treated as a tangent with its contact point at infinity. After the conic is constructed, axes and umbilics can be found via rotating the generating arms and using circle intersections; the center O then yields the principal axes and other invariants.
